cmds.cmd: SELECT * FROM table;
SELECT col1, col2 FROM table;
SELECT DISTINCT col FROM table;
SELECT * FROM table WHERE col = "value";
SELECT * FROM table WHERE col IN (1, 2, 3);
SELECT * FROM table WHERE col BETWEEN 10 AND 20;
SELECT * FROM table WHERE col LIKE "%pattern%";
SELECT * FROM table WHERE col IS NULL;
SELECT * FROM table WHERE a = 1 AND b > 5;
SELECT * FROM table ORDER BY col DESC LIMIT 10;
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM table;
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT col) FROM table;
SELECT SUM(col), AVG(col) FROM table;
SELECT MIN(col), MAX(col) FROM table;
SELECT category, COUNT(*) FROM table GROUP BY category;
SELECT category, SUM(amount) FROM table GROUP BY category HAVING SUM(amount) > 1000;
SELECT col, COUNT(*) FROM table GROUP BY col ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC;
SELECT * FROM a INNER JOIN b ON a.id = b.a_id;
cmds.desc: Only rows that match in both tables

cmds.cmd: SELECT * FROM a LEFT JOIN b ON a.id = b.a_id;
cmds.desc: All rows from a, matched from b

cmds.cmd: SELECT * FROM a RIGHT JOIN b ON a.id = b.a_id;
cmds.desc: All rows from b, matched from a

cmds.cmd: SELECT * FROM a FULL OUTER JOIN b ON a.id = b.a_id;
SELECT * FROM a CROSS JOIN b;
SELECT a.name, b.email FROM users a JOIN contacts b USING (user_id);
SELECT * FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id;
cmds.desc: Self join — table joined to itself

cmds.cmd: INSERT INTO table (col1, col2) VALUES ("a", 1);
INSERT INTO table (col1) VALUES ("a"), ("b"), ("c");
INSERT INTO table SELECT * FROM other WHERE x = 1;
UPDATE table SET col = "new" WHERE id = 1;
UPDATE a SET col = b.val FROM b WHERE a.id = b.a_id;
DELETE FROM table WHERE id = 1;
TRUNCATE TABLE table;
cmds.desc: Remove all rows quickly (cannot rollback in most DBs)

cmds.cmd: CREATE TABLE users (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100), created_at TIMESTAMP);
cmds.desc: Create table with columns and types

cmds.cmd: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email VARCHAR(255);
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN email;
ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN old TO new;
DROP TABLE users;
CREATE INDEX idx_email ON users(email);
cmds.desc: Create index to speed up queries

cmds.cmd: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_email ON users(email);
DROP INDEX idx_email;
SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN (SELECT user_id FROM orders);
SELECT * FROM users WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE user_id = users.id);
WITH active AS (SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = 1) SELECT * FROM active;
SELECT name, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) FROM scores;
SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY date) FROM items;
SELECT name, LAG(value) OVER (ORDER BY date) FROM data;
SELECT category, AVG(price) OVER (PARTITION BY category) FROM products;
cmds.desc: Avg per category as window function

cmds.cmd: SELECT CONCAT(first, " ", last) FROM users;
SELECT UPPER(name), LOWER(email) FROM users;
SELECT LENGTH(name) FROM users;
SELECT SUBSTRING(name, 1, 3) FROM users;
SELECT TRIM(name) FROM users;
SELECT REPLACE(name, "old", "new") FROM users;
SELECT NOW(), CURRENT_DATE, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
SELECT DATE_TRUNC("month", created_at) FROM users;
SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM created_at) FROM users;
SELECT COALESCE(col, "default") FROM table;
SELECT CASE WHEN x > 0 THEN "+" ELSE "-" END FROM data;
